## Heat capacity, internal energy, enthalpy and entropy of each species (`cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R`) {#sec-ch03-species-functions}

### Summary

Every mixture total of this chapter is a sum over species of a concentration times a molar function of temperature:
a heat capacity, an internal energy, an enthalpy or an entropy. This section gives those per-species functions.
Gases and condensates differ in three places: a gas has $c_p = c_v + \mathcal R$ and a condensate $c_p = c_v$; a
gas's enthalpy adds $z \mathcal R T$ to its internal energy; and a condensate's entropy is not read from data but
computed from the condition that each condensation reaction is in equilibrium on its saturation curve.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Molar $c_v$, $c_p$, $u$, $h$, $s$ per species, @eq-ch03-species-functions-u to
@eq-ch03-species-functions-scond.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$] in; each function divided by $\mathcal R$ out.

**Placement.** Called by every `compute` conversion that returns an energy, an entropy or a heat capacity.

**Activation.** Always. Optional per-species extra functions; `use-nasa9-cp` and `use-h2-cp` replace $c_v$, $c_p$
and $u$ for the species they cover.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact (pointwise closed forms, one small linear solve for condensate entropy).

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Symbols of the notation table (@sec-appa): $c^{\star}_n$, $u^{\star}_n$, $s^{\star}_n$, the YAML keys `cv_R` [-], `u0_R` [K] and
`s0_R` [-]; $c_{v,n}$ [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$], $u_n$, $h_n$ [J mol$^{-1}$], $s_n$ [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$], the molar
functions; $K_r$, saturation constant of reaction $r$ in Pa units; $T_\star$ [K], $p_\star$ [Pa], the reference state
of @sec-ch03-reference-state; $c_n$, $z_n$, $N_{\mathrm g}$ as in @sec-ch03-eos. Local symbols: $c_{p,n}$, molar heat
capacity at constant pressure [J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$]; $\nu_{nr}$, stoichiometric coefficient of species $n$ in
reaction $r$, negative for a reactant [-].

### Derivation

**Internal energy and heat capacities.** With a constant heat-capacity coefficient, the molar internal energy that
equals $\mathcal R u^{\star}_n$ at $T_\star$ is

$$
\frac{u_n(T)}{\mathcal R} = u^{\star}_n + c^{\star}_n (T - T_\star) + e_n(T) ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-u}

where $e_n(T)$ is an optional per-species extra function, zero unless C++ code registers one: no YAML key fills
an extra-function slot, `populate_thermo` pads them with empty names and the Python bindings do not expose them (verified by reading at the pin). @eq-ch03-species-functions-u is
computed in `eval_intEng_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_intEng_R >}}), with the constant
$u^{\star}_n - c^{\star}_n T_\star$ stored once as the offset at $T = 0$ (@sec-ch03-reference-state). Its
temperature derivative is the heat capacity at constant volume,

$$
\frac{c_{v,n}}{\mathcal R} = c^{\star}_n + \frac{\mathrm d e_n}{\mathrm d T} ,
$$

computed in `eval_cv_R` ({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cv_R >}}), which calls the derivative of the extra
function under the name of the function with `_ddT` appended. For an ideal gas, $h = u + \mathcal R T$ gives
$c_p = c_v + \mathcal R$; a condensate has $c_p = c_v$. `eval_cp_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_cp_R >}}) adds 1 to $c^{\star}_n$ for the gases only, plus a separate
optional extra function for $c_p$.

**Enthalpy.** For a gas the code writes $h_n = u_n + z_n \mathcal R T$, and for a condensate
$h_m = \mathcal R [u^{\star}_m + c^{\star}_m (T - T_\star)] + \mathcal R\, \zeta_m(T)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{h_n}{\mathcal R} &= \frac{u_n}{\mathcal R} + z_n T, \quad n < N_{\mathrm g}, \\
\frac{h_m}{\mathcal R} &= u^{\star}_m + c^{\star}_m (T - T_\star) + \zeta_m(T), \quad m \ge N_{\mathrm g} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-h}

Here $\zeta_m$ is the condensate entry of the same `czh` function slot that holds $z_n$ for a gas; it is zero
unless set, so by default a condensate's enthalpy equals its internal energy (no $p v$ work for a phase of zero
volume). @eq-ch03-species-functions-h is computed in `eval_enthalpy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_enthalpy_R >}}). The condensate line does not include the extra function
$e_m$ of @eq-ch03-species-functions-u (verified by reading `eval_enthalpy_R` at the pin).

**Gas entropy.** For an ideal gas with constant $c_p$, integrating $\mathrm d s = c_p\, \mathrm d T / T -
\mathcal R\, \mathrm d p_n / p_n$ from $(T_\star, p_\star)$ to $(T, p_n)$ with the partial pressure $p_n = x^{\mathrm
g}_n p$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{s_n}{\mathcal R} &= s^{\star}_n + \frac{c_{p,n}}{\mathcal R} \ln \frac{T}{T_\star} - \ln \frac{p}{p_\star}
- \ln x^{\mathrm g}_n + \sigma_n(T, p) , \\
x^{\mathrm g}_n &= \frac{c_n}{\sum_{k<N_{\mathrm g}} c_k} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas}

where $x^{\mathrm g}_n$ is the mole fraction among gases only and $\sigma_n$ an optional extra function. The code
stores $s^{\star}_n - (c^{\star}_n + 1)\ln T_\star + \ln p_\star$ once and adds $(c^{\star}_n + 1) \ln T - \ln p$
with $T$ in K and $p$ in Pa. @eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas is computed in `eval_entropy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=1 >}}). $x^{\mathrm g}_n$ is clamped at $10^{-300}$ before
the logarithm.

**Condensate entropy.** A condensation reaction $r$ is in equilibrium when its Gibbs energy change vanishes:

$$
\sum_n \nu_{nr} \left( h_n - T s_n \right) = 0 .
$$

Split the gas entropy into its pressure-free part $\tilde s_n$ and the partial-pressure term,
$s_n = \tilde s_n - \mathcal R \ln p_n$. At saturation the product of the reactant partial pressures is the
saturation constant, $\sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} (-\nu_{nr}) \ln p_n = \ln K_r(T)$, with $p_n$ in Pa. Substituting and
dividing by $\mathcal R T$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \sum_n \frac{\nu_{nr} h_n}{\mathcal R T} - \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\nu_{nr} \tilde s_n}{\mathcal R}
+ \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{nr} \ln p_n - \sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \frac{\nu_{mr} s_m}{\mathcal R} , \\
\sum_{m \ge N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{mr} \frac{s_m}{\mathcal R} &= \sum_n \frac{\nu_{nr} h_n}{\mathcal R T}
- \sum_{n<N_{\mathrm g}} \nu_{nr} \frac{\tilde s_n}{\mathcal R} - \ln K_r(T) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-species-functions-scond}

One row per reaction gives a linear system for the condensate entropies; the matrix is the condensate block of
$\nu_{nr}$, transposed. @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond is solved in the second `eval_entropy_R`
({{< code src/thermo/eval_uhs.cpp eval_entropy_R overload=2 >}}) with a Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse, so a
condensate that appears in no reaction gets zero entropy, and more reactions than condensates are solved in the
least-squares sense. The data key `s0_R` of a condensate is not used.

All five functions are exact closed forms; the only numerical step is the pseudo-inverse, exact up to round-off for
a full-rank block. The executable check is not written yet.

### Numerical method

Each function is evaluated pointwise over a tensor of cells, with the species as the last dimension. The optional
extra functions are dispatched per species through a tensor iterator (`call_func2`, `call_func3`), on CPU or CUDA.
The pseudo-inverse of the condensate block is formed once per call from the stoichiometry matrix and broadcast over
the cells.

The species-function figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the per-species functions. {#tbl-ch03-species-functions-code}

Walk-through. (1) `eval_intEng_R` adds the offset, $c^{\star}_n T$ and the extra function, then, when enabled,
replaces the entries of the NASA-9 species and of H$_2$. (2) `eval_cv_R` and `eval_cp_R` do the same for the heat
capacities. (3) `eval_enthalpy_R` builds on `eval_intEng_R` for gases only. (4) `eval_entropy_R` with the
`SpeciesThermo` argument returns gas entropies and zeros for condensates; with the `ThermoOptions` argument it also
solves @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond, which needs the reactions' saturation functions. Setup checks a user can
hit: both `eval_entropy_R` refuse a `conc` or `stoich` whose species dimension is not $N_{\mathrm g}$ plus the
number of condensates.

The NASA-9 and H$_2$ options replace $c_v$, $c_p$ and $u$, but not the gas entropy, which keeps the constant
$c_{p,n} = \mathcal R (c^{\star}_n + 1)$ of @eq-ch03-species-functions-sgas (verified by reading both
`eval_entropy_R` at the pin).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | with `use-nasa9-cp`, $c_p$, $c_v$ follow the polynomial | $10^{-10}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | with it, finite-difference $\mathrm d u/\mathrm d T$ equals $c_v$ | $10^{-6}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | NASA-9 and constant $u$ agree at 300 K | $10^{-12}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | without it, $c_p/\mathcal R = c^{\star} + 1$, $c_v/\mathcal R = c^{\star}$ | $10^{-14}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_h2_cp.py` | H$_2$ $c_p$ in both modes against reference values | $2 \times 10^{-3}$ abs. | not yet derived |

: Tests of the per-species functions. {#tbl-ch03-species-functions-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin. No test checks @eq-ch03-species-functions-scond directly:
the condensate entropy is exercised only through the adiabat test of @sec-ch03-adiabat. That is missing evidence.

### Limits

With `use-nasa9-cp` or `use-h2-cp`, the entropy keeps a constant $c_p$ while $u$, $h$ and $c_p$ do not, so the
functions are not mutually consistent for those species (verified by reading; the size of the effect is not
measured). The condensate enthalpy ignores the extra internal-energy function. A condensate that appears in no
reaction has zero entropy.
